tasks.title: Implement Mana API Type Interfaces
tasks.objective: Create the three core API interfaces that define contracts for mana consumers, creators, and storage entities. These interfaces form the foundation for mod integration.
constraints: Interfaces must be pure Java with no Minecraft or Fabric dependencies
Interfaces must be in the com.manacore.core.api.types package
Do not add implementation classes, only interfaces
Do not modify any existing source files
Use only standard Java types in interface signatures

client_server_considerations.authority: server is authoritative for all mana operations

acceptance_criteria: ManaConsumer.java defines methods for consumer behavior (e.g., gather radius, onManaReceived)
ManaCreator.java defines methods for creator behavior (e.g., injection radius, mana production rate)
ManaStorage.java defines methods for storage behavior (e.g., capacity, stored amount, insert/extract)
All interfaces compile with pure Java (no Minecraft imports)
Executable tests pass verifying interface contracts
tasks.rationale: The API type interfaces are the foundational contracts that enable mod integration. They must exist before any implementation of consumers, creators, or storage. These are pure Java interfaces with no dependencies on Minecraft, making them ideal for isolated testing. This task advances the MVP by providing the type system that example blocks and entities will implement.

tasks.title: Implement Mana Event Data Classes
tasks.objective: Create the three event data classes for mana flow, gather, and store events. These enable event-driven integration for mods.
constraints: Event classes must be pure Java with no Minecraft or Fabric dependencies
Event classes must be in the com.manacore.core.api.events package
Use immutable data classes (records or final classes)
Do not add event bus or handler logic, only data classes
Do not modify any existing source files

client_server_considerations.authority: server is authoritative for event generation

acceptance_criteria: ManaFlowEvent.java captures flow data (source/target positions, amount, direction)
ManaGatherEvent.java captures gather data (center, radius, amount gathered)
ManaStoreEvent.java captures storage data (entity/block ID, amount, operation type)
All event classes are immutable and compile with pure Java
Executable tests pass verifying event construction and field access
tasks.rationale: Event data classes enable event-driven architecture for mods to react to mana system changes. These are pure data structures with no behavior, making them simple to implement and test in isolation. This task depends on API types only if event fields reference those interfaces; otherwise it can be parallel. It advances the MVP by providing the data structures for the event system described in the architecture.

tasks.title: Implement Mana Configuration System
tasks.objective: Create the server configuration class for mana system parameters including flow rates, gather radii, and storage limits.
constraints: Config class must be pure Java with no Minecraft or Fabric dependencies
Config class must be in the com.manacore.core.config package
Configuration values must have sensible defaults
Do not implement file I/O or serialization, only the data class
Do not modify any existing source files
acceptance_criteria: ManaConfig.java defines configuration fields for flow, gather, and storage parameters
All configuration values have non-negative defaults
Config class provides validation for all fields
Class compiles with pure Java (no Minecraft imports)
Executable tests pass verifying default values and validation
tasks.rationale: Configuration system is essential for server-side tuning of mana parameters. This is a self-contained data class with validation logic, perfectly suited for isolated pure-Java implementation and testing. It has no dependencies on other new components, advancing the MVP by providing the parameterization needed for flexible server configuration.
